fields.acceptance: Unit tests in the package that parses .rhiza/dispatch.toml cover: no file or no [[schedules]] giving no schedules; an entry with every and workflow and one with cron and command read with defaults catch_up once and overlap skip; a file with both [request] and [[schedules]] reading both with no error; an unknown table still failing with an error naming it; each error case (unknown key, duplicate name, every with cron, neither workflow nor command, bad cron, every 30s, catch_up = "all", overlap = "parallel") failing with an error naming the schedule and the key; and a testscript where rhiza check passes on a repo whose .rhiza/dispatch.toml holds [request] and [[schedules]]
fields.statement: Rhiza reads [[schedules]] entries from the repo's committed .rhiza/dispatch.toml beside its [request] and [ready] dispatch tables, widening the tables that file allows to those three (amending dispatch-rules-file's rule that any other table is an error, so [[schedules]] is no longer one): each entry has a name unique in the repo, exactly one of every and cron, exactly one of workflow and command, and optionally catch_up (once, the default, or skip) and overlap (skip, the default, or queue); any other key, a duplicate name, both or neither of a pair, an unparsable every or cron, or an unknown catch_up or overlap value is an error naming the schedule and key, and any table other than [request], [ready] and [[schedules]] is still an error naming it

fields.acceptance: Tests in internal/api with a fake clock show a daemon poll over two projects starting each due schedule's run, a due schedule waiting while maxRuns is full and then firing once, an unresolvable workflow starting nothing with a log line naming the schedule, and the daemon log carrying a scheduled run's start and its failure; for a scheduled command run that starts and fails, no Rex call is made
fields.statement: The daemon serving the root reads every registered project's schedules on each poll and starts each due schedule's run, taking a slot under rhiza.daemon.maxRuns and the project's maxRuns like any run; a due schedule with no free slot waits for one and still fires once, a schedule whose file no longer reads or whose workflow no longer resolves starts nothing and is logged; it logs each scheduled run's start, end and result, and Rhiza opens no Rex tab or pane of its own for a scheduled run, its start or its failure (failures go to the daemon log); an agent step inside a scheduled workflow opens its session as in any headless daemon run
